title: The Mountain Finally Yields
theme: A day of career-best rounds up and down the field, crowned by a new course record, while the Wooden Spoon found a fresh occupant.
tone: Wry British understatement, treating a golf course record and a Wooden Spoon handover with identical solemnity.
opening_hook: Two visits after Penha Longa's slopes first punished the field, its mountainside finally yielded — to one man's iron game, and to nobody else's.

round_story.subject: Gregg Williams sets a new Penha Longa course record with a gross 82
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the best gross round of Gregg Williams's entire TEG career and a new course record at a venue that had previously resisted everyone, extending his overnight leads in both the TEG 15 Trophy and the TEG 15 Green Jacket.
round_story.shape: Williams arrives at Penha Longa already leading both races; two immaculate stretches, birdies at the 8th and 10th sandwiching tidy pars either side, carry him fourteen shots inside his own previous best at the course; he finishes with a gross 82, a new course record beating the previous mark of 86, and both his leads swell further.
headline_candidates: A New Best For Penha Longa
Williams Rewrites The Penha Longa Record Book
round_story.standfirst: An 82 gross, fourteen shots better than his own previous best around the Sintra hills, is the finest round of Gregg Williams's TEG career and leaves both his races looking healthier than ever.

race_story.subject: The Wooden Spoon changes hands as Alex Baker collapses and Stuart Neumann recovers
race_story.why_it_matters: Stuart Neumann had been rooted level at the foot of the TEG 15 Wooden Spoon table since round two; a ruinous back-nine stretch from Alex Baker hands him the cellar outright by fourteen shots, in what is the third-worst Trophy round of Alex Baker's 35-round TEG career.
race_story.shape: Neumann enters the round tied for last with nowhere to go but up; three holes from the 12th to the 14th cost Alex Baker twelve shots outright, including a lone sextuple bogey at the par-4 14th, while Neumann quietly banks nine points across holes 14 to 16; by the close the Spoon has swapped hands entirely, with Neumann clear and Baker installed in last by fourteen shots.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Inherits The Wooden Spoon
Neumann Escapes As Baker Falls Last
Wooden Spoon Swaps Hands In Sintra
race_story.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Inherits The Wooden Spoon
race_story.standfirst: A ruinous stretch from the 12th to the 14th, capped by a double-figure score at the par-4 14th, hands Alex Baker sole occupancy of the Wooden Spoon cellar as Stuart Neumann's revival lifts him clear.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's wild first look at Penha Longa
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: On his maiden visit to the course, John Patterson's card swung from a run of six holes worth 19 stableford points to two separate double-figure blow-ups, a volatility that captures how mercilessly Penha Longa punishes any lapse.
discovered_storylines.shape: Patterson opens steadily before catching fire from the 3rd to the 8th, banking 19 points in six holes; the turn sours almost immediately as a quadruple bogey at the 10th and a quintuple bogey at the 16th bracket a bleeding three-hole stretch from the 9th; he still finishes with a respectable tally, but the card reads like two entirely different rounds.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Nineteen points in six holes and two separate double-figure scores summed up a first look at the Sintra hills for John Patterson, whose scorecard swung wildly all afternoon.

race_state_note: Gregg Williams's Trophy and Green Jacket leads both grew again but the order at the top is unchanged from overnight; the meaningful movement was at the foot of the Wooden Spoon table, where Alex Baker replaces Stuart Neumann.
